Question: Two integers have a sum of \(26.\) When two more integers are added to the first two integers the sum is \(41.\) Finally when two more integers are added to the sum of the previous four integers the sum is \(57.\) What is the minimum number of even integers among the \(6\) integers?
Solution:
Subtracting successive totals tells us that the three pairs have sums
\[
26,\qquad 41-26=15,\qquad 57-41=16.
\]
The middle pair has an odd sum. Two odd integers have an even sum, as do two even integers, so this pair must contain one odd integer and one even integer. Thus at least one of the six integers is even.

To show that one even integer is enough, choose the pairs
\[
(11,15),\qquad (7,8),\qquad (3,13).
\]
Their sums are \(26\), \(15\), and \(16\), giving the required successive totals \(26\), \(41\), and \(57\). Only \(8\) is even. Therefore the minimum is \(1\), choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
